key_insight: Combining clinical, tumor genomics, and ctDNA data with machine learning modestly improved progression-free survival risk prediction for HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer.
clinical_relevance: This multimodal approach may help better identify patients at higher or lower risk of progression, supporting more informed prognostic assessment in advanced breast cancer.
method: Trained fusion-based machine learning models on baseline clinical, ctDNA, and gene expression data from MONALEESA-2, -3, and -7.
Compared early fusion, late fusion, and single-modality models for progression-free survival prediction.
Evaluated performance in a held-out test set using Kaplan-Meier, Cox, and Weibull analyses.
evidence_signal: In the test set (n=382), the late fusion model achieved C-index 0.727, slightly better than early fusion (0.718) and single-modality approaches, with clear low- vs high-risk separation.
watch_item: The gains over simpler models were modest, so external validation and real-world testing are needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Clinical and Genomic Prognostic Factors for Progression-Free Survival in Metastatic Breast Cancer Using Phase III MONALEESA Trials
